headline: Ohio Expands Rare Wetland Protection With New 118-Acre Addition
meta_description: Ross County seeks to add 118 acres to nature preserve around Kinnikinnick Fen, potentially growing protected habitat to 450 acres total.
summary_short: Ohio commissioners voted to support acquiring 118 acres around a rare wetland. If funded, the protected habitat could grow from its current size to 450 acres.
body:
Ohio's Ross County commissioners have voted to support acquiring 118 acres of land surrounding the Kinnikinnick Fen and Herron Downs nature preserve. The September 8 vote by the Ross County Board of Commissioners signals formal backing for the project, which would create a protective buffer around both the preserve and Kinnikinnick Creek.

If funding materializes through Ohio's Clean initiative, the protected habitat could expand to 450 acres—a significant growth for this rare wetland ecosystem. A local family has offered to donate its house and three additional properties to support the acquisition, demonstrating community commitment to the conservation effort.

The Ross County Park District is leading the effort to bring the vision to completion. Success would secure long-term protection for the wetland and its surrounding watershed, benefiting both wildlife and water quality in the region.
quick_facts: 118 acres targeted for addition to Ohio nature preserve
Protected habitat could grow to 450 acres if fully funded
Ross County commissioners voted September 8 to support acquisition
Project includes Kinnikinnick Fen and Herron Downs preserve
Local family offering to donate house and three properties
